questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black letters means no passing zone. You will see it on the left side of a two-lane road where you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: How much space should you leave between your car and the car in front of you?

options.text: One second
Three to six seconds
10 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Three to six seconds
questions.explanation: Leave three to six seconds of space between your car and the car ahead in normal conditions. Leave more space when driving faster.

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you arrive at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, what should you do?

options.text: Yield to the vehicle on your left.
Yield to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until there are no vehicles before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: The vehicle on your right has the right-of-way at an uncontrolled intersection when you arrive at the same time. Then proceed in the order vehicles arrived.

questions.question: The light is green, but traffic is blocking the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking your way, even if your light is green. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block other traffic and get a ticket.

questions.question: You are in the center lane of an expressway and cars keep passing you on both sides. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Use the right lane on expressways unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than other traffic, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: You want to turn left at the next corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians waiting on the sidewalk for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all pedestrians, bicycles, and vehicles coming toward you on their green light.

questions.question: What is true about bicyclists?

options.text: They should ride facing traffic.
They must stay in the right lane.
They must follow the same traffic laws as drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must follow the same traffic laws as drivers.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists must obey the same traffic laws as car drivers. The same right-of-way rules apply to both.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black letters warn drivers about hazards ahead. Round signs are only used for railroad crossings.

questions.question: How can you help cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane.
questions.explanation: Move to another lane when possible to create space for cars entering the freeway. If you cannot move lanes, adjust your speed to let them merge safely.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to go through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to turn green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always override traffic lights and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
Slow-moving vehicle.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for people with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for vehicles with disability license plates or disability placards.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic light mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
Your protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means your protected turn is ending. Be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no vehicles are coming. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: You are on an interstate and cars are merging from the on-ramp on your right. What is the best thing to do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead on an interstate, move left when safe to give merging cars room.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to scan for hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for possible hazards. Do not stare only at the road directly in front of your car. Scan ahead and watch for vehicles around you.

questions.question: You must tell MVD about an address change within:

options.text: 10 days.
30 days.
45 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 days.
questions.explanation: You must notify MVD of any change in your name or address within 10 days of the change.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
Left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, be in the lane closest to the centerline. Start your turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut the corner. Turn into the first legal lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard signals you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are near a school. Stay alert and stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
Stop if you are going the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are traveling.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus picking up or dropping off children, you must stop completely before reaching the bus. This applies no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: If you parallel park facing downhill:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels away from the curb.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the road edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 have zero tolerance for alcohol. Any trace of alcohol in your system will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles pass you on the right. If a driver behind you wants to go faster, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane so traffic flows smoothly.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for faster driving, passing, or turning left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic, entering the road, or turning right.

questions.question: The best way to avoid danger while driving is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always keep your eyes on the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of your surroundings. Watch the front, sides, and rear of your vehicle. This helps you spot problems early and change speed or position as needed.

questions.question: If you want to enter the freeway but don't see a gap in traffic, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: If you don't see a gap to enter the freeway, slow down on the ramp to wait. Do not drive to the ramp's end and stop, as you will not have room to speed up before entering traffic.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping immediately, even in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with a siren and flashing lights, drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again once the vehicle passes.

questions.question: In fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may drive too close.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When crossing a sidewalk from an alley or driveway to enter traffic, drivers should:

options.text: Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect pedestrians to let you pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, stop before entering the sidewalk or road. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your judgment and makes your reflexes unreliable.

questions.question: At night, lower your high beam headlights when within this distance of a car ahead:

options.text: 500 feet.
100 feet.
200 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: 200 feet.
questions.explanation: When driving at night, switch your high beams to low beams when you are within 200 feet of another vehicle ahead of you.
